newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower on social order concerns.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower on social order concerns.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed sharply lower on Monday as dealers feared that concerns over crime on the island may have begun to trigger a capital outflow.
The local unit closed at T$27.720 against Saturday's T$27.667 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a hectic US$351.5 million.
More than 50,000 demonstrators staged a march on Sunday to protest against the government's failure to curb violent crime following the recent kidnap and murder of a famous actress's daughter.
Another 40 college students held an anti-crime rally outside the cabinet building in Taipei on Monday.
"If the protests turn into real social disorder, then you would continue to see the local dollar depreciate," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said there was heavy buying of the greenback from foreign commercial banks.
"The greenback buying came in the form of non-delivery forward buying," another dealer said.
A T$27.69-$27.76 range was seen in Tuesday trading.
